key_insight: EvoPINN turns PINN design into an execution-grounded search process, using an LLM agent to discover executable algorithms and architectures that outperform hand-engineered baselines on PDE tasks.
engineering_relevance: For solid mechanics and other physics simulations, this suggests a practical path to automate model and training design while preserving numerical validity and scientific constraints.
method: Decouples neural representation from training program to create a modular search space.
Uses an LLM agent to iteratively propose memory-conditioned program modifications.
Filters candidates with strict structural verification and budget-matched PDE evaluation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive tests across oscillatory, elliptic, dissipative, and nonlinear transport PDE regimes, with EvoPINN reducing relative L2 error and inventing SLRC-PINN, which remained strong under parameter-matched comparison.
watch_item: The approach may be sensitive to the quality of verification, evaluation budgets, and search design, so gains could depend on careful experimental setup and not transfer uniformly to all PDE problems.
paper_title: EvoPINN: Agentic Discovery of Executable Algorithms for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
